For Loop Number Check

for_loop_nb_check.Rd

Verify that the sequence expression of every for construct of a function is written with hard numbers, i.e., only integer-valued numeric literals joined by : (like 1:3, 0:0, -3:-1 or 1e3, each of them possibly reduced to a single literal like 3), each literal possibly negated by a unary minus, or a base::seq_len(...) or base::seq_along(...) call. Any other writing is reported, notably 1:length(x) (recommended replacement: base::seq_along(x = x)), 1:n with n a variable, 1:(n - 1), 1:2.5, 1:NA, 1:Inf or 1:TRUE, and plain variables like for(i in x) or calls like base::rev(x = x), base::names(x = df) or base::seq(x = x).

Indeed, for instance x <- 0 ; for(i in 0:0){y <- i} makes one loop while it should a priori not be necessary, and x <- character() ; for(i in 1:length(x)){y <- i} returns y = 0, because 1:length(x) gives c(1, 0) when x is empty. Thus, base::seq_along(x = ...) should be used instead of length(x).

Usage

for_loop_nb_check(
  x,
  export = FALSE,
  out_path = ".",
  safer_check = TRUE,
  lib_path = NULL,
  error_text = ""
)

Arguments

x

a function name, written without quotes and brackets.

export

Single logical value. Export the modified function (see the @returns and @details sections) into a .R file? If TRUE, the modified code is written in a file named <function name>_safer.R (the function name is the last component of the submitted name, so that pkg::fun() gives fun_safer.R) in the directory indicated by the out_path argument, and NULL is returned: the modified function is only available in the file. The file contains an assignment of the modified function: <function name>_safer <- function(...) ..., so that base::source()ing it recreates the modified function. An error is returned if this file already exists, and if the tested function is not designated by a function name (like test or package::test), i.e., written by an inline definition (like function(x){x}) or by a component writing (like FUN_LIST$fun). Nothing is written if no modification is performed (everything clean, or no checking line inserted). If FALSE (default), the modified function is returned by return() (NULL if no modification is performed).

out_path

Single character string indicating the absolute pathway of the folder where to export the modified function when the export argument is TRUE. out_path = "." (default) means the R working directory set by the user. Ignored if the export argument is FALSE.

safer_check

Single logical value. Perform some "safer" checks? If TRUE, checkings are performed before main code running (see the safer-r project): 1) correct lib_path argument value 2) required functions and related packages effectively present in local R libraries and 3) R classical operators (like "<-") not overwritten by another package because of the R scope. Must be set to FALSE if this function is used inside another "safer" function to avoid pointless multiple checkings.

lib_path

Vector of characters specifying the absolute pathways of the directories containing the required packages for the function, if not in the default directories. Useful when R packages are not installed in the default directories because of lack of admin rights. More precisely, lib_path is passed through the new argument of .libPaths() so that the new library paths are unique(c(new, .Library.site, .Library)). Warning: .libPaths() is restored to the initial paths, after function execution. Ignored if NULL (default) or if the safer_check argument is FALSE: only the pathways specified by the current .libPaths() are used for package calling.

error_text

Single character string used to add information in error messages returned by the function, notably if the function is inside other functions, which is practical for debugging. Example: error_text = " INSIDE <PACKAGE_1>::<FUNCTION_1> INSIDE <PACKAGE_2>::<FUNCTION_2>.". If NULL, converted into "".

Value

A table-like text message indicating the for sequences not written with hard numbers or a message saying that everything seems fine, printed by base::message() (always, whatever the value of the export argument).

Table-like: column 1, the line number in the function code (starting at the "<- function" line, i.e., without counting the #' header lines); column 2, the construct (for); column 3, the code preceding the construct body.

In addition, the returned value depends on the export argument and on the presence of reported for sequences. If export is FALSE and at least one checking line has been inserted (see the @details section), the modified function is returned by return(). If export is TRUE, NULL is returned (invisibly), and the modified code is only available in the exported file, whose location is indicated by a message. NULL is also returned when no modification is performed (everything clean, or no checking line inserted).

Details

The reported for sequences are the ones whose computed controller depends on objects or function results, i.e., whose number of iterations is not predictable from the writing itself. The modification consists in adding a checking line before each reported for construct (see below).

More precisely, for_loop_nb_check() verifies that the sequence expression written between in and the closing parenthesis of the condition of each for construct is exactly a hard-number writing or a seq_len(...) or seq_along(...) call. The hard-number writing is: an optional unary minus, then a numeric literal, then optionally :, then an optional unary minus, then a numeric literal, with nothing else (e.g., 1:3, 0:0, -3:-1, 1e3, 1L:3L, 0x10:0x11, or single literals like 3 or -3). Each numeric literal must be finite and integer-valued: 2.5, 1e-3, NA, NaN, Inf and TRUE/FALSE are reported (they are silently truncated toward 0, or run for a very long time, at execution). A seq_len(...) or seq_along(...) call (namespaced or not, whatever the arguments, because these functions are the recommended safe replacements) is clean only if it occupies the whole sequence expression: seq_along(x) - 1 is reported, because it gives c(0, 1) when x has 2 elements. Any other writing is reported: variables like for(i in n) or for(i in x), function calls like 1:length(x), 1:nrow(df), 1:(n - 1), 1:3 - 1 (which gives c(-2, -1) at execution), 2 - 1, 1:3:1, base::rev(x = x), base::seq(x = x) or base::names(x = df). Comments and strings are ignored during this verification.

Deliberately NOT reported, because these writings are fully determined by the code itself: their control is the responsibility of the writer, and no checking line is added for them: the equal-bounds (like 0:0 or 1:1), both-negative (like -3:-1) and decreasing (like 1:0) hard-number writings.

Each reported for construct is modified in the recovered code: the sequence expression is evaluated once in a specific object named tempo_for_seqN (N being the rank of the report), this object is checked, and then used as the for controller, giving tempo_for_seqN <- <SEQUENCE> ; <CHECKS> ; for(<VARIABLE> in tempo_for_seqN)<BODY>. Evaluating the sequence expression once in the tempo_for_seqN object guarantees that the checking and the for controller are strictly identical. At execution, base::warning() is issued when the computed sequence is empty (0 iteration), contains NA values, has a single value (equal bounds), contains infinite values, or is decreasing (like 1:0). The errors of the sequence evaluation itself (like 1:NA or 1:Inf) are propagated as they are. Warning: no endless loop is possible with Inf, because R fully evaluates the for controller before iterating: 1:Inf gives an error at evaluation, and an Inf element just gives one iteration with i = Inf, whatever a potential break in the loop body. The modification is performed at the exact positions of the reported for constructs in the recovered code, so that comments, strings and the formatting of the original code are preserved outside the modified spans. When the reported for construct is not preceded by a statement boundary (unbraced body of if/else/for/while/repeat, assignment value, function argument, operator operand, etc.), the whole modified construct is wrapped in curly brackets, because a statement insertion would otherwise break the binding of the enclosing writing. When export is FALSE, the modified function is returned by return() in a new environment whose parent is the environment of the submitted function: please, check the returned function before replacing the original one, notably because its environment is not necessarily the same. When export is TRUE, the modified code is written in the file <function name>_safer.R of the directory indicated by the out_path argument, and nothing is written if no modification was performed. Warning: the exported file is a standalone R script containing the modified function code, and its potential pre-existing version is never overwritten (an error is returned instead). Warning: the x argument must be designated by a function name, not by an inline function definition (like function(x){ x }), when export is TRUE, otherwise the name of the exported file cannot be determined.

Warning: the checking lines are not inserted when the tempo object name (tempo_for_seqN) is already used anywhere in the checked function code (including in comments and strings), or when a reported for construct is located inside the sequence expression of another reported for construct (overlapping insertion spans): the concerned for constructs are listed in the returned message, and remain unmodified. The checking lines are also not inserted, for the same reason (listed in the message), when a for construct that requires the wrap in curly brackets (see above) contains comments in its span (the wrap collapses the construct on a single line, which would merge the comments with the code), or when such a construct shares the end of its body with a for construct written after it and also requiring the wrap (as in for(a in 1:n) for(b in 1:length(x)){...}, where the two bodies end at the same position: the wrap of the latter, applied first, moves the shared closing token away from the position where the former would end its own body).

Warning: aliased bounds like n <- length(x) ; for(i in 1:n) cannot be detected, because n is a plain variable in the for writing. The checking must then be done on the function body.

The returned line numbers are indicative, depending on which source is checked. For instance, saferDev::colons_check (compiled) has not the same line numbers as its source file. Notably, compiled functions do not have comments anymore, compared to the same source function sourced into the working environment. In addition, the counting starts at the "<- function" line, i.e., without counting the #' header lines potentially present in source files.

Examples

# Warning: these examples may not work well when using the "Run examples" link 
# because of a particular environment. Please, copy-paste in a local environment.
# See also https://safer-r.github.io/saferDev/articles/for_loop_nb_check.html
fun1 <- function(x){ for(i in 1:3){ base::print(x = i) } }
saferDev::for_loop_nb_check(fun1)
#> 
#> 
#> AFTER RUNNING saferDev::for_loop_nb_check().
#> INSIDE fun1(), EVERYTHING SEEMS CLEAN.
#> 
#> NULL
fun2 <- function(x){ for(i in 1:length(x)){ base::print(x = i) } } ; saferDev::for_loop_nb_check(fun2)
#> 
#> 
#> 
#> INSIDE fun2(), SOME for() SEQUENCES ARE NOT WRITTEN WITH HARD NUMBERS:
#> 
#> LINE	CONSTRUCT		CODE
#> 3	for		for (i in 1:length(x)) {
#> 
#> MODIFIED FUNCTION RETURNED BY return().
#> 
#> function (x) 
#> {
#>     tempo_for_seq1 <- 1:length(x)
#>     if (base::length(x = tempo_for_seq1) == 0) {
#>         base::warning("FOR SEQUENCE EMPTY: 0 ITERATION", call. = FALSE, 
#>             immediate. = FALSE, noBreaks. = FALSE, domain = NULL)
#>     }
#>     else if (base::anyNA(x = tempo_for_seq1)) {
#>         base::warning("FOR SEQUENCE WITH NA VALUES", call. = FALSE, 
#>             immediate. = FALSE, noBreaks. = FALSE, domain = NULL)
#>     }
#>     else if (base::length(x = tempo_for_seq1) == 1) {
#>         base::warning("FOR SEQUENCE WITH A SINGLE VALUE (EQUAL BOUNDS?): SINGLE ITERATION", 
#>             call. = FALSE, immediate. = FALSE, noBreaks. = FALSE, 
#>             domain = NULL)
#>     }
#>     else if (base::is.atomic(x = tempo_for_seq1) && base::any(base::is.infinite(x = tempo_for_seq1), 
#>         na.rm = TRUE)) {
#>         base::warning("FOR SEQUENCE WITH INFINITE VALUES: NO ENDLESS LOOP POSSIBLE BECAUSE THE for() CONTROLLER IS FULLY EVALUATED BEFORE ITERATING, BUT CHECK THAT AN INFINITE VALUE IS EXPECTED", 
#>             call. = FALSE, immediate. = FALSE, noBreaks. = FALSE, 
#>             domain = NULL)
#>     }
#>     else if (base::is.atomic(x = tempo_for_seq1) && base::typeof(x = tempo_for_seq1) %in% 
#>         base::c("double", "integer") && base::all(x = tempo_for_seq1 < 
#>         0, na.rm = FALSE)) {
#>         base::warning("FOR SEQUENCE WITH ALL NEGATIVE VALUES", 
#>             call. = FALSE, immediate. = FALSE, noBreaks. = FALSE, 
#>             domain = NULL)
#>     }
#>     else if (base::is.atomic(x = tempo_for_seq1) && base::typeof(x = tempo_for_seq1) %in% 
#>         base::c("double", "integer", "character", "complex") && 
#>         base::length(x = tempo_for_seq1) >= 2 && tempo_for_seq1[1] > 
#>         tempo_for_seq1[2]) {
#>         base::warning("FOR SEQUENCE DECREASING", call. = FALSE, 
#>             immediate. = FALSE, noBreaks. = FALSE, domain = NULL)
#>     }
#>     for (i in tempo_for_seq1) {
#>         base::print(x = i)
#>     }
#> }
#> <environment: 0x555f06abaa50>
fun3 <- function(x){ for(i in base::seq_along(x = x)){ base::print(x = i) } } ; saferDev::for_loop_nb_check(fun3)
#> 
#> 
#> AFTER RUNNING saferDev::for_loop_nb_check().
#> INSIDE fun3(), EVERYTHING SEEMS CLEAN.
#> 
#> NULL
fun4 <- function(x){ for(i in 1:length(x)){ base::print(x = i) } } ; fun4_safer <- saferDev::for_loop_nb_check(x = fun4, export = FALSE, safer_check = TRUE, lib_path = NULL, error_text = "") # modified function returned (checking line added)
#> 
#> 
#> 
#> INSIDE fun4(), SOME for() SEQUENCES ARE NOT WRITTEN WITH HARD NUMBERS:
#> 
#> LINE	CONSTRUCT		CODE
#> 3	for		for (i in 1:length(x)) {
#> 
#> MODIFIED FUNCTION RETURNED BY return().
#> 
fun5 <- function(x){ for(i in 0:0){ base::print(x = i) } } ; saferDev::for_loop_nb_check(x = fun5, export = FALSE, safer_check = TRUE, lib_path = NULL, error_text = "") # NULL returned: the degenerate hard-number writings are the responsibility of the writer, no checking line inserted
#> 
#> 
#> AFTER RUNNING saferDev::for_loop_nb_check().
#> INSIDE fun5(), EVERYTHING SEEMS CLEAN.
#> 
#> NULL
